_comment: Which secrets the 1Password vault 'Context' supplies to this repo's GitHub
Environments. Read by .github/workflows/sync-secrets.yml, whose header
explains the flow and the one hazard: an 'optional' key ABSENT from the
vault is DELETED from the GitHub environment, so adding a name here that
nobody has put in 1Password removes a value somebody set by hand.
The rule for choosing a list: 'required' is anything a deploy is broken
without, so a missing value should fail the sync loudly rather than
produce a half-configured deployment. 'optional' is anything whose
absence is a real, working state the product documents.
The five desktop-signing values are optional by that rule rather than by
hope: with none of them deploy-desktop.yml builds an UNSIGNED dmg, which
installs on the machine that built it, is refused by Gatekeeper anywhere
else, and is given no system audio by macOS. The workflow prints a warning
saying so. CSC_LINK is a Developer ID certificate as base64 and
CSC_KEY_PASSWORD its passphrase; ASC_API_KEY_P8, ASC_KEY_ID and
ASC_ISSUER_ID are an App Store Connect key for notarisation. None of them
exists yet — they are Apple credentials only the account holder can
create — and the day they do, dispatching that workflow signs with no
code change.
APPLE_TEAM_ID and EAS_PROJECT_ID are account identifiers, not credentials
— but this repository is public and MIT licensed, and CLAUDE.md is
explicit that no internal hostname or account identifier belongs in it,
so they are synced like anything else rather than committed. ASC_APP_ID
selects the existing App Store Connect record for non-interactive submits
and is required for that release path. APPLE_TEAM_ID
is optional: it is read by deploy-mobile-native.yml only when submitting
to iOS (EXPO_APPLE_TEAM_ID), and a build with submit=false or
platform=android needs it not at all. EAS_PROJECT_ID is required: every
workflow that runs `eas build`, `eas update` or `eas deploy` fails its own
preflight without it (see apps/mobile/app.config.js).
The two Stripe values are optional by the rule above, and the absence is a
documented working state rather than a hope: with no STRIPE_PRICE_ID a
deployment sells nothing and the Premium section says so, and with no
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET the webhook refuses every delivery — which is the
only safe direction, because 'unconfigured means allow' would be a free
upgrade for anybody who can find the URL. STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is NOT here:
it is a credential the staff console holds in `appSecrets`, encrypted at
rest and rotatable, exactly as SEARCH_D1_API_TOKEN is, and it never
becomes a deployment environment variable. See docs/decisions/billing.md.
